preview: Today, we look at a quiet change in office design: some companies are bringing back desks assigned to individual workers. The issue is not only where people sit, but what kind of work environment companies want to create. Why can a desk matter to a worker’s sense of belonging and ability to concentrate? And how does this change fit with the wider move toward shared office space?
comment_1: Listen for why some employees are unhappy with using any desk that is free.
comment_2: Workers are not always happy with hot-desking because the office can feel less predictable. So, are some companies moving away from shared desks?
comment_3: This story shows a tension between personal workspaces and shared desks. Some companies are bringing back assigned desks, while hot-desking remains more common than before the pandemic. Next, we will look more closely at this change from two angles.
comment_4: So, assigned desks may be linked to how connected and focused workers feel. But they are returning only in some workplaces, while desk sharing remains the larger trend. Now, let’s bring these two points together.
